verdictSummary: SSCTR-P31-F02 is closed on the paths the rule names (W1, W2, W4 RED on R7D-FREEZE-2 and clean on the candidate; the relation ASK reaches every event kind; clinical first holds; no double application; the single-break path is preserved; differential contained). One MAJOR instrument/runtime conflict must be resolved instrument-side before the freeze runs: the pre-registered P17 RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK relation fails on the candidate for the interface-documented flow 'correction of an applied break while a newer break is kept' (QE-R7D-P32-01). Four MINOR residuals and one TEST_GAP set must be disclosed with owners. No blocker.

On R7D-FREEZE-2 the same matrix applies returns or validates. keptAsk is first in decide; only the clinical route, the previous-validity guard, the factual re-plan's own ask and an unrecognised-choice ask precede it, all non-dose. heldByRunGap returns any ASK whose question is not UNREPORTED_TRAINING unchanged (code, line 373). Same input gives byte-identical output (probe RP; T8; DETERMINISM relation clean on four extra cases; probe outputs identical across two runs). Record-order invariance fails only for declarations with equal clocks (QE-R7D-P32-02).

Re-run: 145 cases, 141 identical, 4 differing (DEV-22 to DEV-25), 0 unexplained; rows identical to the committed DIFFERENTIAL_VS_R7D_FREEZE_2.json. The 140 single-break cases identical support the byte-identical single-break claim, which code reading also supports (keptBreaks with one group reproduces retainedBreak; readBreak extraction is line-for-line; keptEpisode, separate and notApplied are unset on that path).

findings.finding: Instrument/runtime conflict on the interface-documented flow 'correction of an applied break while a newer break is kept' (the SSCTR p4b path). The runtime reads a kept correction of an applied break as not read: the next plain review applies the kept break and records the correction in notApplied, VALID. The same correction stated again by that review is asked (CORRECTION_ACROSS_KEPT_BREAK), REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION. So the pre-registered P17 metamorphic relation RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK (BLOCKER, no envelope, unchanged by R7D-PREREG-4 Delta 2) fails on the candidate: a final holdout containing this flow would fail P17 on designed behaviour. Validation 4 has no development case for it, so its no-false-block result does not reach it. Also, after the kept break's return the correction is never asked again (the next reviews KEEP and GATED_NEXT_STEP, VALID): the ASK text 'a correction of an earlier break across it is then asked' holds only if the athlete re-sends it. Dose-neutral in the probe (the comparator that applies the correction first still gives the kept break SHORT 7 days), and fail-closed in the restated variant. Any live runtime design differs from RESTATE here (asking on every review while the correction is kept never lets the kept break be applied), so the reconciliation is instrument-side.

findings.finding: Record-order dependence for declarations with equal clocks. Groups are ordered by first declaredAt and the head by end then declaredAt; ties fall back to the carried record's array order. A 14-day holiday (unnamed) and a 7-day trip with the same end (named) declared at the same instant: record order [holiday, trip] applies a separate-breaks return (14 days, MODERATE, episode = trip); order [trip, holiday] asks INTERRUPTION_RELATION (the holiday becomes the later unnamed break). Same input, same output (determinism holds); record-position invariance does not. Fail-closed in one order, no dropped fact in either. R7D-FREEZE-2 was order-invariant here (both orders re-entered from the latest). Not reachable by the evaluation client, which carries the record in step order.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe-p32-probes.mjs <scratch root>, scenario ORD (out-probes.candidate.json: order1 REESTABLISH, order2 ASK INTERRUPTION_RELATION, sameStopAndEntry false). Harness form (two steps at the same time): probes/qe-p32-p18-false-block.mjs QE-FB-4, all properties and relations clean.

findings.finding: The exact-replay key (facts apart from episodeId) omits the time a dateless report is anchored to. Two dateless reports with equal facts ({days:5, WORK, nonclinical}) declared two weeks apart are joined as one declaration: no relation question, and the older report has no effect (one SHORT 5-day return from the newer). The dated control asks INTERRUPTION_RELATION. Dose-equivalent under the disclosed QE-R7D-P31-12 reading (a dateless kept break ends the day before the review that applies it, so as separate breaks both would overlap at the same days); the outcome equals R7D-FREEZE-2's. Invisible to the harness: P18 joins them by the same key and (a) is not evaluable without dates.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe-p32-probes.mjs, scenario DL (candidate: plain review REESTABLISH 2026-12-06..12-10 SHORT; dated control ASK INTERRUPTION_RELATION). probes/qe-p32-p18-false-block.mjs QE-FB-3: P18 NOT_APPLICABLE, no violation.

findings.finding: A report id re-sent with other break facts while its break is kept is read over the kept row in that decision (keptBreaks: mine.i = input.interruption) but never recorded (newDeclaration keeps the first row). (a) It bypasses the no-last-write-wins rule: with the 14-day holiday kept under id X and a named separate trip kept, X re-sent with 7-day facts gives a 7-day SHORT return, where the facts on record (holiday + trip, the days between reported not done) give 21 days MODERATE. (b) The return's separateBreaks entry for X carries the re-sent dates and hash with the first row's declaredAt, unlike the record row. (c) A relation answer sent under the kept report's own id is lost when that decision asks something else (TRAINING_BETWEEN_BREAKS): the next review asks the relation again; under a new id the flow completes (21 days MODERATE). Mechanism pre-existing and disclosed as QE-R7D-P31-10 ('not recorded nor refused'); the consequences (a)-(c) are not disclosed against the Phase 3.2 rule. Not reachable by the evaluation client (one event id per step). Unpinned by any test (judge mutant QM32-14 survives the suite).

R7D-FREEZE-2 gives the same SHORT results in SE (out-probes.R7D-FREEZE-2.json).

findings.finding: Separate-break identities recorded in separateBreaks are not addressable after their return: episodesOf and appliedName know only the return's episode (the head). A correction naming the earlier separate break (its listed episode) is asked as a different interruption that shares days, and the question offers the return's episode; naming that episode with the earlier break's corrected facts replaces the whole stop (21-day stop to 12 days: the later break's days leave the applied stop). Fail-closed until the athlete names the return's episode; a correct consumer path exists (send the whole corrected stop under the return's episode, INTERFACE-4 'send the whole corrected break'), at the price of restating separate facts as one.
findings.reproduction: probes/qe-p32-probes.mjs, scenario SC (namingA: ASK, missing interruption.episodeId, 'its episodeId qe-B'; namingEpisode: REESTABLISH SAME_BREAK 2026-11-16..2026-11-27, 12 days, separateBreaks empty).

findings.finding: Judge mutants of the Phase 3.2 delta: 18 applied, 9 killed by the directed files, 9 survive the whole suite (938/0). Priority: QM32-10 (an earlier separate break whose reason is missing or unclear is read into the stop without the reason question: a possibly clinical cause read as nonclinical), QM32-13 (an earlier separate break with invalid facts read without asking), QM32-06 (a conflicted report between two breaks counted as reported, i.e. read as no training: the SSCTR question 4b behaviour is unpinned). Then QM32-02 (a correction by a chosen name, not an event id, is not joined), QM32-05 (replaying an answering review whose own break is not the head), QM32-14 (same report id re-sent with other facts, QE-R7D-P32-04). QM32-03, QM32-07 and QM32-17 are close to equivalent on reachable inputs. The runtime behaves correctly on these paths by code reading; the gap is that no test pins it.

findings.finding: P18 and INSERT_NEWER_BREAK showed no false block on four constructed cases beyond validation 4 (TRAINING_AFTER answered done, notApplied, dateless equal facts, equal clocks): P18 PASS (3, 3, n/a, 3 units), INSERT clean (1 unit each). INSERT's inserted break (fixed reason text, dates asOf-7..asOf-1, no name) can only be joined to a kept break with byte-identical facts, so a false block from it needs a corpus break with that reason text. P18 mirrors the runtime's grouping (same keys, step order equals record order in the client, replays excluded by event id) and its TRAINING_AFTER branch is a superset of the runtime's trainedBetween. Residual risk: a same-id re-send with other facts, unreachable in the client.

HARNESS-4 text drift: P17's window and RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK still end at 'a later review states a break of its own (it replaces this one)', which no longer holds. Effect: P17 stops following the older break once a newer one is stated, and P18 checks the older break only at a return. No false block results (any VALID decision while both are open still violates the newer break's own P17 window), but the comment is wrong under R7D-PREREG-4.

findings.finding: Freeze tooling: freeze-r7d-3.mjs and verify-r7d-3.mjs join --evidence, --ssctr and --engineering to the repository root, so they must be given repository-relative paths (an absolute Windows path fails). The freeze binds only top-level .mjs/.json/.md files of each review folder and of review probes folders. The verifier rechecks the R7D-FREEZE-2 record but not R7D-FREEZE-1 (the freeze itself refuses if FREEZE-1 changed before it runs).

conditionsForFreeze.condition: QE-R7D-P32-01, before freeze-r7d-3.mjs runs and before any final holdout exists, with no runtime byte changed: reconcile RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK with the Phase 3.2 notApplied rule, for example by not restating a stated correction of an applied break (its episodeId names a recorded return's episode or event) while another stated break is open, recorded as a pre-registration addendum to R7D-PREREG-4 (Delta 2 currently says P17 is unchanged); add a development case of the QE-FB-2 form and show no false block on the candidate, RESTATE still detecting QE-R7D-P3-01 on R7D-FREEZE-1, and all witnesses firing. If the coordinator cannot make an instrument-only change in this phase, the freeze waits for a Chief/Founder disposition of this conflict; the final holdout is not authored until it is resolved. In the same addendum, state precisely that a kept correction of an applied break listed in notApplied is not asked again unless re-sent.

The freeze record's disclosures list QE-R7D-P32-02 to -05 as residuals (P32-03 with QE-R7D-P31-12, P32-04 as an extension of QE-R7D-P31-10), with the consumer conditions: never re-send a report id with other facts; answer INTERRUPTION_RELATION under a new report id; state a break's dates; to correct one break of a separate-breaks return, restate the whole stop under the return's episode. Owner: Chief; trigger: the freeze record.

TEST_GAP QE-R7D-P32-06 recorded with owner Engineering and trigger the next authorized runtime phase (tests cannot be added now without changing the reviewed test bytes): first QM32-10, QM32-13, QM32-06, then QM32-02, QM32-05, QM32-14.
